- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially after dips.
- Model often overshoots after recent price spikes (e.g., 90+), especially when sentiment is positive — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak if sentiment remains positive.
- After strong downward sentiment, model underreacts — forecast should be adjusted upward by 5–10% to account for mean reversion or policy-driven rebounds.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is mixed or positive — apply downward correction if sentiment shifts to neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 1.00), model may overfit recent trends — smooth forecast curve to avoid abrupt reversals.
- When true outcome drops sharply after a forecast peak, model often fails to anticipate policy or supply shocks — add a 5–10% downward buffer if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days.
